## Operating lessons

- **ui-never-settled** (confirmed) — The UI did not publish readable content within the learned budget — screenshot the device before concluding anything about the app.
  - _evidence:_ waited 8s for com.android.settings with no readable dump
- **heads-up-notification-banner-steals-tap-not-just-dump** (seen twice) — A heads-up notification banner overlay can intercept a real tap aimed at an element underneath it and route the touch to the banner's own app instead of the target app. Symptom: read_screen after the tap reports the screen owned by the notification's app package (Messenger, WhatsApp, etc.) with a large unrelated node count. Recovery: press back once to dismiss the wrongly-opened app, then retry the same tap once the banner has cleared.
  - _evidence:_ On legal-about-translated-policy-documents module, tapping the in-app back-arrow app-bar element (id 495_147, "Langue") on the app's Language settings screen instead opened Facebook Messenger's inbox full-screen, because a Messenger notification banner was occupying the top-of-screen region at the moment of the tap. Relaunching the app under test and retrying navigation worked cleanly.
- **ios-no-app-data-clear** (seen twice) — iOS cannot clear an app's data from the host: there is no `pm clear` equivalent, so a persisted login survives between runs. Reset through the app's own sign-out flow instead of assuming a clean start.
  - _evidence:_ clear_app_data(com.google.ios.youtube) is unavailable on the iOS adapter
- **project-device-bound-to-wrong-target** (seen twice) — A native project with no device pin inherits `state.device_serial()` — the serial of whatever run last posted telemetry. A web run posts its URL as that serial, nothing lists a URL, and the 'trust an unlisted serial' fallback in backend/agent_bridge.py:device_for handed the URL to a fresh Android project, so every read_screen/launch failed with "device <url> not online". Fix from the session: the agent cannot repoint it; the user (or Claude Code) pins the project with `POST /projects/<package>/device {"device_serial": "<adb serial>"}` and restarts the server so the session is rebuilt. Root cause patched 2026-08-20: device_for now ignores a URL-shaped live serial for native projects and falls through to the one attached phone.
  - _evidence:_ com.whatsapp.app, 2026-08-20: meta.json was platform=android with no device_serial; adb listed R5CR12GJAJY; the live serial was https://metaesthetics-staging.web.app/ from the prior web suite. Pinning + restart fixed it; regression test test_a_web_runs_url_is_never_borrowed_by_a_native_project added.
- **scroll-with-ime-open-triggers-gboard-glide-typing** (seen twice) — When a text field is focused and the on-screen keyboard is showing, calling scroll can swipe across the keyboard area (scroll uses the screen's vertical middle band, which the IME often occupies) and Gboard interprets it as glide-typing, silently appending stray characters to the focused field. Dismiss the keyboard (tap elsewhere / press back once) before scrolling any screen with a focused input, and re-check the field's actual text with read_screen afterward.
  - _evidence:_ Re-reproduced on Personal Information: tap_xy near a form field opened the keyboard and focused the postal-code EditText; the very next scroll(down) call appended ' G6' to it, turning '8001' into '8001 G6', visible in a screenshot with Gboard still open. Fixed by retyping '8001' with clear=true before it could be saved.
- **wait-for-text-timeout-capped-below-requested** (seen twice) — Confirmed with stronger evidence: wait_for_text(timeout=3600) is NOT a usable sleep primitive for long real-world durations at all. Across 7 consecutive calls with unique never-appearing probe text and timeout=3600, real elapsed wall-clock time (tracked via the status-bar clock in read_screen) was wildly inconsistent and mostly near-zero: one call ~12min, one ~4min, five calls 0min each — total only ~17 minutes across 7 calls that should have taken 7 hours if timeout were honored. There is no reliable way in this toolset to force a genuine deterministic wait of tens of minutes to an hour by looping this call; the number of iterations needed is unbounded and unpredictable. For any test case requiring a real long background/inactivity interval (e.g. a 60-minute session timeout spec), do not attempt to satisfy it by looping wait_for_text — flag it via ask_user as a genuine tooling blocker, and if unanswered (autonomous/unattended run), report the sub-case as explicitly untested/blocked (with whatever partial elapsed time was incidentally observed, clearly caveated) rather than looping indefinitely or fabricating a pass/bug verdict.
  - _evidence:_ Backgrounded com.metaestetics.mobile_clientapp at 6:06pm, made 7 consecutive wait_for_text(timeout=3600, unique impossible text) calls interleaved with read_screen clock checks: 6:06->6:18 (12min), 6:18->6:19 (1min), 6:19->6:19 (0min), 6:19->6:23 (4min), 6:23->6:23 (0min), 6:23->6:23 (0min). Total 17 minutes of real elapsed time across calls that requested 3600s each — no correlation between requested timeout and actual elapsed time.
- **web-native-select-dropdown-unusable** (seen twice) — UPDATE: this is now fixed. On a web project, a native HTML <select> element can be driven by: tap_element to focus it, then type_text with the first letter(s) of the target option — this now sends real keyboard events that trigger the browser's native type-ahead-select behavior, updating the select's value even though the option-list popup itself still isn't clickable via tap_xy (that popup is a browser/OS compositor layer outside the page content, so coordinate clicks on it just dismiss it). After typing the matching letter, press key="enter" (or tap elsewhere) to close the dropdown and confirm the selection via screenshot. This is the reliable path for any <select>/Spinner control on this harness now — do not waste turns on tap_xy coordinate guesses against an open native select popup.
  - _evidence:_ On app.metaesthetics.net's Step 2 Practice Type field (id #practiceType, a native select rendered as 'Spinner'), tap_element to focus + type_text('A') selected 'Aesthetic Medicine' and highlighted it in the still-open list; pressing enter closed the dropdown and the field permanently showed 'Aesthetic Medicine' afterward, confirmed via screenshot. Earlier in this same session, identical type_text('A') attempts had no effect before a harness-side fix was applied mid-session.
- **testing-agent-no-gmail-tool-access** (seen once) — Even when Gmail MCP tools (mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__*) appear as loadable via ToolSearch and their schemas load successfully, the testing agent role is blocked from calling them at invocation time with "is not available to the testing agent. Drive the phone with the device tools; use Read/Write only for screenshots, memory and the report." Do not plan a test case around reading the user's real inbox directly — if a case needs verification-code delivery confirmed, either ask_user to relay the code/confirm receipt, or note the limitation and report what the app's own UI showed (e.g. whether it presented a code-entry step at all) as the observable evidence instead.
  - _evidence:_ ToolSearch successfully loaded mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__search_threads' full schema mid-session (it appeared in the functions block), but calling it immediately returned an error blocking it for this agent role, on a task that explicitly asked to verify real email delivery to mrsiyam1604@gmail.com.
- **web-credential-name-value-mismatch** (seen once) — On this project (metaesthetics-staging.web.app), list_credentials returned two names — the account's own email address ("qa.mira.20260812@metaesthetics-test.com") and a descriptive slug ("test-clinic-account"). Intuition says the email-shaped name holds the email and the slug holds the password, but it is backwards: use_credential("qa.mira.20260812@metaesthetics-test.com") types the real password ("QaTest123!") and use_credential("test-clinic-account") types a non-password description string ("Signup & Login already made a new clinic") that fails login. Don't assume credential name shape maps to field type — reveal the password field (tap 'Show password') and read_screen once to confirm the actual typed value before concluding a login failure is an app bug.
  - _evidence:_ Typing the 'test-clinic-account' credential into the password field produced 'Invalid email or password' twice; revealing the field showed its literal value was the sentence 'Signup & Login already made a new clinic', not a password. Typing the email-named credential into the same field instead produced 'QaTest123!' and logged in successfully.
- **web-harness-no-file-upload-primitive** (seen once) — This web-testing harness (Playwright-backed) has no tool to actually select/inject a file into an <input type=file> or a "Change image"/drag-drop upload zone — there is no upload_file/set_input_files/attach_file tool in the exposed toolset, and clicking the trigger opens a native OS file chooser outside the DOM that read_screen and screenshot cannot see or interact with (the page dump is unchanged before/after the click). Any test case requiring an actual image/file upload (valid image display, dimension rejection, file-type rejection, oversized-file rejection, AI auto-fix behavior) cannot be executed end-to-end with this toolset. Flag such cases as blocked/untested rather than guessing a pass or bug, and check whether the upload zone's own on-screen copy (accepted formats, size limits, disclaimers like 'any size allowed') gives testable evidence without needing a real file.
  - _evidence:_ On clinic-web's Edit Practitioner > Personal Information tab, clicking the 'Change image' button under 'Profile Photo (any size allowed)' produced zero DOM change — read_screen before and after the click returned byte-identical touchable-element lists and text, and screenshot showed no dialog, no file picker, no loading state. No tool named upload_file/set_input_files/attach_file exists in the available toolset (confirmed via ToolSearch for 'upload file image attach').
- **web-harness-no-tab-switch-primitive** (seen once) — This web-testing harness (Playwright-backed) has no tool to switch to or inspect a newly opened browser tab — when a link has target="_blank" (e.g. an external Terms & Conditions link), tapping it may open a new tab but read_screen/screenshot keep showing the original tab unchanged. This is indistinguishable from the link being silently non-functional. Flag such cases as unverified/warning rather than guessing pass or bug, the same way file-upload and audio-injection gaps are already handled.
  - _evidence:_ Tapped 'General Terms & Conditions for Clinics' (an external-link-styled button with a new-tab icon) on the Join Existing Clinic form; read_screen and screenshot showed the exact same Step 1 form afterward with zero change, no way to confirm whether a new tab opened with the real document or nothing happened at all.
- **web-owner-warning-trailing-slash-false-positive** (seen once) — On a web project, read_screen's "owned by X, not the app under test (Y)" warning can fire even when X and Y are the same origin, differing only by a trailing slash (e.g. owner `https://app.metaesthetics.net` vs. project url `https://app.metaesthetics.net/`). Don't treat the warning alone as proof of a wrong window on web — check the dump's actual text/elements first; a trailing-slash-only mismatch is a harness string-compare artifact, not a real overlay.
  - _evidence:_ Launched https://app.metaesthetics.net/, read_screen returned the correct login page content (Log In, Create New Clinic Group, etc.) but still warned "owned by `https://app.metaesthetics.net` (69 nodes), not the app under test (`https://app.metaesthetics.net/`)" — same origin, only the trailing slash differs.
